hardware_backed_credential_storage_used.title: Hardware-Backed Credential Storage Used
hardware_backed_credential_storage_used.description: Attested true when tokens/credentials on this untrusted device are stored exclusively in the OS-protected, ideally hardware-backed keystore (iOS Keychain / Secure Enclave, Android Keystore / StrongBox, or EncryptedSharedPreferences) rather than in plaintext SharedPreferences, NSUserDefaults, plist, SQLite, or sandbox files. When false the credentials are recoverable from a lost, stolen, or rooted device, which is exactly this exposure. Maps to dossier config_surface 'local_credential_storage_hardware_backed' (secure_value=hardware_backed_keystore). MASVS-STORAGE-1 / MASVS-CRYPTO secure key storage.

tokens_in_plaintext_device_storage.title: Tokens In Plaintext Device Storage
tokens_in_plaintext_device_storage.description: Interpreted true when tokens, session credentials, or secrets are observed persisted in cleartext in app-readable device storage — SharedPreferences XML, NSUserDefaults, plist, plaintext SQLite, caches, or sandbox files — outside the keystore. Modeled as a positive interpreted boolean (fired with is_true) so detection is polarity-safe by construction and never pattern-matches a composite storage string. Corresponds to the insecure_value 'plaintext_or_app_readable_storage' of dossier 'local_credential_storage_hardware_backed'.

encrypted_at_rest.title: Sensitive Data Encrypted At Rest
encrypted_at_rest.description: Shared workspace attestation: sensitive data (PII, tokens, secrets) persisted on the device outside the keystore is encrypted at rest with a key held in the keystore (e.g. AES-GCM under a Keystore-held key), rather than written as cleartext caches/logs/temp files/WebView storage. Fires (is_false) when cleartext sensitive data is present at rest. Reuses the cross-cutting encrypted_at_rest vocabulary; maps to dossier config_surface 'no_sensitive_data_in_cleartext_at_rest' (secure_value=encrypted_or_absent). MASVS-STORAGE-2 / MASVS-CRYPTO-1.

tls_only_transport.title: TLS-Only Transport Enforced
tls_only_transport.description: Attestation: all app-to-backend traffic is carried over TLS only, with cleartext transport impossible (Android Network Security Config cleartextTrafficPermitted=false / iOS App Transport Security left on, NSAllowsArbitraryLoads not set). True on a hardened mobile client. When false, the channel can fall back to cleartext HTTP and a rogue/user-installed CA on the hostile device can MITM and intercept tokens and PII in transit (MASVS-NETWORK-1). Shared workspace vocabulary — name matches the gateway/dataFlow transport facet.

cleartext_http_permitted.title: Cleartext HTTP Permitted
cleartext_http_permitted.description: Interpreted boolean over the composite transport-trust config (Android cleartextTrafficPermitted, iOS NSAllowsArbitraryLoads / NSExceptionAllowsInsecureHTTPLoads): true when the app is configured to permit cleartext HTTP to the backend (or a broad insecure-HTTP exception). Fires the exposure because permitted cleartext lets the hostile-device adversary read/alter the channel. Modeled as an interpreted boolean rather than a raw substring match so the secure baseline (cleartext denied) stays silent (MASVS-NETWORK-1).

certificate_pinning_enabled.title: Certificate Pinning Enabled
certificate_pinning_enabled.description: Attestation: the app pins the backend's certificate/public key (Android <pin-set> SHA-256 SPKI pins with a backup pin; iOS URLSession delegate / pinning lib), so a malicious CA or user-installed root on a compromised/rooted device cannot transparently MITM the channel. True on a hardened client. When false the app relies on system trust only and a user-installed root CA on the hostile device intercepts TLS and harvests tokens/PII (MASVS-NETWORK-2).

server_certificate_validated.title: Server Certificate Validated
server_certificate_validated.description: Attestation: the mobile client fully validates the backend server certificate chain (no disabled hostname verification, no trust-all/accept-any TrustManager or insecure URLSession delegate). True on a hardened client. When false, certificate validation is bypassed and any presented certificate is accepted, enabling trivial MITM regardless of pinning or TLS. Shared workspace vocabulary — name matches the dataFlow certificate-validation facet.

root_jailbreak_detection_enabled.title: Root/Jailbreak Detection Enabled
root_jailbreak_detection_enabled.description: Interpreted boolean: true when the app detects a rooted/jailbroken runtime and gates or restricts sensitive flows on a positive verdict (defence-in-depth, MASVS-RESILIENCE-1). False fires this exposure — the app runs identically on a rooted/jailbroken device with no check or response, so OS sandbox guarantees protecting the keystore and screen are silently undermined. Assessor interprets per dossier config key 'jailbreak_root_detection' (secure: detected_and_responded, insecure: no_detection).

server_verified_app_integrity_attestatio.title: Server-Verified App Integrity Attestation
server_verified_app_integrity_attestatio.description: Interpreted boolean: true when the backend server-side verifies the request comes from a genuine, untampered instance of the real app on a genuine device before trusting it — Android Play Integrity (deviceIntegrity MEETS_DEVICE_INTEGRITY/MEETS_STRONG_INTEGRITY, appLicensingVerdict LICENSED) and/or iOS App Attest (DCAppAttestService Secure-Enclave assertion validated server-side) — and the app resists tampering/repackaging. False fires this exposure — the server trusts any client claiming to be the app, leaving a repackaged forged app indistinguishable from the genuine one. Consolidates the jailbreak/attestation and repackaging vectors' server-verified app-integrity facet. Maps to dossier config key 'device_app_attestation' (secure: server_verified_attestation, insecure: no_attestation); MASVS-RESILIENCE.

secrets_hardcoded_in_config_or_iac.title: Secrets Hardcoded In App Binary Or Config
secrets_hardcoded_in_config_or_iac.description: Shared workspace concept: long-lived API keys, signing secrets, or backend shared secrets are embedded in the app binary/resources (APK/IPA) or its bundled config rather than provisioned at runtime over an authenticated channel. On a hostile device an attacker decompiles the package on their own hardware and recovers any such secret by string/entropy analysis. Fires when secrets are present in the binary (insecure); the assessor confirms via static analysis of the decompiled package (dossier: anti_tamper_no_hardcoded_secrets — insecure_value hardcoded_secrets_present). MASVS-RESILIENCE / MASVS-CODE; OWASP Secrets Management.

access_token_ttl_minutes.title: Access Token TTL (Minutes)
access_token_ttl_minutes.description: Lifetime of the mobile session's access token in minutes. Short-lived tokens (minutes) bound the replay window of a token stolen off a lost or compromised device; long-lived tokens let a stolen bearer token be replayed until expiry. The exposure fires when the TTL exceeds the short-lived threshold. (RFC 9700 OAuth 2.0 Security BCP; OAuth BCP for native apps.)

sender_constrained.title: Access Token Sender-Constrained
sender_constrained.description: Whether the access token is sender-constrained (bound to the device's key via DPoP per RFC 9449 or mTLS per RFC 8705) rather than a plain bearer token. When false, a token exfiltrated from device storage/logs can be replayed verbatim from attacker hardware. Shared workspace vocabulary attribute. The exposure fires when sender-constraint is absent (is_false).

refresh_token_rotation_enabled.title: Refresh Token Rotation Enabled
refresh_token_rotation_enabled.description: Whether refresh tokens are rotated on use with reuse-detection (RFC 9700). Without rotation, a stolen refresh token mints fresh access tokens indefinitely and replay goes undetected. Shared workspace vocabulary attribute. The exposure fires when rotation is absent (is_false).

server_side_revocation_supported.title: Server-Side Token Revocation Supported
server_side_revocation_supported.description: Whether the backend exposes a server-side revocation/logout path that immediately invalidates a device's access and refresh tokens (e.g. on reported device loss/theft). Without it, stolen-token access persists until natural expiry with no recovery — recovery must be server-side because the org cannot manage the unmanaged device. Shared workspace vocabulary attribute. The exposure fires when no revocation path exists (is_false).

excluded_from_device_backup.title: Sensitive Data Excluded From Device Backup
excluded_from_device_backup.description: Attested true when sensitive data (tokens, credentials, PII) is excluded from OS/cloud device backups — Android android:allowBackup="false" or backup/dataExtractionRules excluding secret stores, and iOS Keychain items using a ...ThisDeviceOnly accessibility class so they are never written to iCloud/iTunes backups. False (the firing/insecure state) means secrets ride into backups (allowBackup=true, not ThisDeviceOnly) and can leak to an attacker who restores or harvests the backup.

screen_capture_protection_enabled.title: Screen Capture Protection Enabled
screen_capture_protection_enabled.description: Attested true when sensitive screens block screenshots/screen-recording and resist overlay/tapjacking — Android sets WindowManager.LayoutParams.FLAG_SECURE on sensitive windows (plus filterTouchesWhenObscured), and iOS hides/blurs sensitive content in the app-switcher snapshot. False (the firing/insecure state) means sensitive screens are freely screenshot, recorded, or overlaid, leaking displayed secrets/PII.

sensitive_clipboard_hygiene.title: Sensitive Clipboard & Keyboard Hygiene
sensitive_clipboard_hygiene.description: Attested true when secret-entry fields enforce clipboard/keyboard hygiene — secrets are not auto-copied to the shared (cross-app, long-lived) clipboard and secret fields use secure/no-suggestion input types (iOS isSecureTextEntry / autocorrectionType=.no; Android inputType textNoSuggestions/textPassword). False (the firing/insecure state) means passwords/tokens are placed on the shared clipboard or cached by the keyboard, where other apps on the device can read them.

secrets_masked_in_logs.title: Secrets Masked In Logs
secrets_masked_in_logs.description: Shared-workspace attribute: attested true when credentials, tokens, and PII are excluded/masked from device logs (logcat / NSLog / crash-reporting SDKs) and debug logging is stripped from release builds. False (the firing/insecure state) means secrets are written to device logs that are readable on a rooted device or harvested by crash-reporting services (CWE-532).

deep_link_origin_validated.title: Deep Link Origin Validated
deep_link_origin_validated.description: Interpreted boolean: deep-link / custom-URL-scheme / intent handlers validate the origin and parameters of the inbound link and re-check authorization server-side before acting. True when handlers treat the link as untrusted input and verify it; false (the firing/insecure state) when a crafted link or intent can drive a sensitive action or leak data without origin/authorization checks. (MASVS-PLATFORM.)

deep_link_url_scheme_validation.title: Deep Link / URL Scheme Validation
deep_link_url_scheme_validation.description: Real config-surface property (dossier deep_link_url_scheme_validation): whether inbound deep links / custom URL schemes / intents are validated and authorized. Secure value 'validated_authorized' (handlers validate origin+params, prefer verified App Links, minimize exported components). Fires on the insecure value 'unvalidated_deep_links' where a crafted link/intent triggers sensitive actions or leaks data without checks. (MASVS-PLATFORM.)

server_side_allowlist_validation.title: Server-Side Allowlist Validation
server_side_allowlist_validation.description: Shared workspace-vocabulary interpreted boolean: the backend re-validates every request from the untrusted mobile client with allow-list input validation and authorization independent of any client-side gate. True when server-side allow-list validation is enforced; false (the firing/insecure state) when the backend relies on client-supplied input being well-formed or on the app to enforce business rules. (OWASP Input Validation; trust-boundary principle.)

client_asserted_state_trusted_serverside.title: Client-Asserted State Trusted Server-Side
client_asserted_state_trusted_serverside.description: Interpreted boolean: whether the backend trusts client-asserted state (entitlements, prices, identifiers, geofence/jailbreak/integrity claims) supplied by the mobile app. True (the firing/insecure state) when the server trusts client-side flags or client-supplied business state, so a tampered or instrumented app can bypass enforcement; the secure posture is false — client claims are advisory and the server is the authority. (Trust-boundary principle; OWASP Input Validation.)

biometric_local_auth_gates_secrets.title: Biometric/Local-Auth Gates Secrets
biometric_local_auth_gates_secrets.description: Interpreted attestation: access to keystore-held secrets and sensitive in-app actions is gated behind a device biometric/local-auth challenge (Android BiometricPrompt before key use; iOS Keychain items with a biometry-bound SecAccessControl, e.g. .biometryCurrentSet). True when a local-auth challenge is genuinely required before secrets are usable; false (the exposure) when secrets/sensitive actions are usable with no biometric/local-auth challenge, so an attacker with a momentarily-unlocked or stolen device can exercise stored credentials. Maps to dossier config_surface 'biometric_local_auth_gating' (secure=biometric_gated_keys, insecure=no_local_auth); MASVS-AUTH local-auth.

keys_bound_to_user_authentication.title: Keystore Keys Bound To User Authentication
keys_bound_to_user_authentication.description: Interpreted attestation: keystore keys protecting secrets are cryptographically bound to user authentication so the OS will not release/use them without a fresh local-auth challenge (Android keys created with setUserAuthenticationRequired(true); iOS SecAccessControl with biometry/userPresence so the Secure Enclave enforces presence). True when keys are auth-bound; false (the exposure) when keys are created without setUserAuthenticationRequired / without a biometry-bound SecAccessControl, leaving keys usable on a stolen unlocked device. Distinct facet of dossier 'biometric_local_auth_gating' covering the key-binding mechanism rather than the action gate.
